events.title: Vivaldi browser launched
events.summary: Vivaldi 1.0 shipped on April 12, 2016 — a feature-rich browser from former Opera CEO Jon von Tetzchner, built for power users who missed classic Opera.
events.about: Vivaldi packed tab stacking, built-in notes, split-screen views, and deep customization into a Chromium shell. It targeted the niche of users who wanted a browser as a productivity tool, not a minimal chrome bar — continuing Opera's power-user legacy after Opera switched to Blink.

narrative.whyChosen: Vivaldi kept the spirit of classic Opera alive after its pivot to Chromium.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved there was still room for boutique browsers with extreme customization.
narrative.problemSolved: Opera veterans wanted a browser with tabs, mail, and widgets without giving up modern engine compatibility.

events.title: Node.js 6 released
events.summary: Node.js 6.0.0 shipped on April 26, 2016 with V8 5.0, improved Buffer API, and the foundation for the first modern LTS schedule.
events.about: Node 6 became LTS in October 2016 — the stable line for Express, React SSR, and early webpack ecosystems. Long-term support commitments gave enterprises confidence to standardize on Node for APIs and build tooling.

narrative.whyChosen: Node 6 established the even-numbered LTS pattern teams still follow today.
narrative.whyImportant: Formal LTS let companies plan multi-year Node deployments.
narrative.problemSolved: Production teams feared odd-numbered Node releases would break without warning.

events.title: Andy Jassy named AWS CEO
events.summary: Amazon named Andy Jassy CEO of Amazon Web Services in April 2016 — formalizing his leadership of the cloud division he built since 2003.
events.about: Jassy grew AWS from an internal infrastructure experiment into the template for modern cloud computing — EC2, S3, and managed services changed how startups and enterprises deploy software.

narrative.whyChosen: Jassy led the business that defined public cloud infrastructure.
narrative.whyImportant: AWS made on-demand compute and storage the default deployment model for new software.
narrative.problemSolved: Teams bought servers months in advance instead of scaling elastically with demand.
